'''Martijn Bernard Katan''' (born 1946) is a Dutch nutritionist, an emeritus professor at the [[Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]] and author of two popular science books on nutrition.

==Early life==
Katan was born in [[Arnhem]] in 1946.<ref name=nrc>{{cite news|author=Jannetje Koelewijn |url=https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2016/04/14/we-doen-te-heilig-over-groente-en-fruit-1609643-a1397225 |url-access=subscription |title='We doen te heilig over groente en fruit' |newspaper=NRC |language=nl |publisher=NRC Handelsblad |date=14 April 2016 |access-date=26 October 2020}}</ref> 

== Education ==
He studied chemistry and biochemistry at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. He obtained his PhD in [[molecular biology]] in 1977 under [[Piet Borst]] from the same university.<ref name="nrc" /> 

== Career ==
Katan started working at [[Wageningen University]] in 1976 where he researched "Nutrition and risk factors for cardiovascular disease".{{Citation needed|date=October 2020}} In 1998, he was appointed professor of human nutrition at the university.<ref name="nrc" /> He was also the "Nutrition Foundation Professor" at the [[University of Nijmegen]] from 1985 to 1998. Between 1998 and 2003 he was scientific director of the Nutrition and Health program of the Wageningen Centre for Food Sciences.{{Citation needed|date=October 2020}}

In 2003 Katan became a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/5914 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200730103947/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/5914 |title=Martijn Katan |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=30 July 2020}}</ref> In 2005 he moved from Wageningen University to the [[Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]] where he was appointed professor of nutrition.<ref name=nrc/> Katan is a member of the [[Dutch Health Council]].

He took up emeritus status in 2011.<ref>{{cite news|author=Mac van Dinther |url=http://www.volkskrant.nl/wetenschap/-groenten-verwacht-er-niet-te-veel-van~a4287577/?hash=6452125f663ab4aac9dad8203eebc9d9eb61f956 |title='Groenten: verwacht er niet te veel van' |language=nl |newspaper=[[de Volkskrant]] |date=23 April 2016 |accessdate=23 April 2016}}</ref>

In 2022, he was elected a member of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Martijn Katan|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Katan_Martijn|work=Member|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2024-09-26}}</ref>

==Research==
Katan's research focuses on the relationship between nutrients and their effects on the heart. Katan gained notoriety for his research on cholesterol and [[trans-fat]]s.<ref name=nrc/> He demonstrated, among other things, that boiled coffee creates a cholesterol burden that filtered coffee does not. His research on the harmful effects of trans-fatty acids has encouraged the food industry to minimize the use of trans-fats in the food supply.<ref>{{cite web|author=Sander Becker |url=https://www.ad.nl/wetenschap/niet-politiek-correct-ik-vertel-wat-waar-is~a7886518/ |title='Niet politiek correct? Ik vertel wat waar is' |language=nl |publisher=Algemeen Dagblad |date=28 January 2011 |accessdate=16 October 2020}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=October 2020}}
* 2001: The Epstein Award; [[American Heart Association]] Council on Epidemiology 
* 2003: European Nutrition Award; Federation of European Nutrition Sciences. 
* 2004: European Lipid Science Award; European Federation for the Science and Technology of Lipids.
* 2005:, named by the Thomson Society (formerly the [[Institute for Scientific Information]]) as a Highly Cited Researcher "in the art of Agricultural Science," which means that he is among the 250 most cited scientists in that field

* ''Voedingsmythes. Over valse hoop en nodeloze vrees''. (2016). Uitgeverij Bert Bakker.
